subject: Action plan & eval — clarifications on overage policy and burst rate
messages:
From: Olivia Huntley <olivia@huntleyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Eval plan + MAP questions (burst caps / overage rates)

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team is enthusiastic and we want to move toward a short evaluation with clear success criteria. A couple quick asks from product and procurement before we lock the mutual action plan: 

- Can you confirm how overage/burst billing will be calculated during the 30-day evaluation? We expect a spike as we run synthetic load and some parallel ingestion jobs.
- Is there any temporary cap we can set during the eval to prevent surprise invoices?
- We’d like the rate card for bursts (1.5x, 2x, 5x) and an example invoice calculation for ~2M tokens at a 3x spike.

If possible please send a draft MAP and a short SOW so procurement can review. Procurement (procurement@huntleyhealth.com) will need a DocuSign-ready SOW to route internally.

Appreciate it — aim is to close the eval contract and be ready to start by Dec 1st if everything looks good.

Best,
Olivia Huntley
VP Product, Huntley Health
[Attachment: requirements_deck.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Huntley <olivia@huntleyhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Eval plan + MAP questions (burst caps / overage rates)

Hi Olivia — great to hear the team wants to move quickly. I put together a short MAP and rate card excerpt attached and answered your bullets below. Attaching: MAP_Huntley_v1.pdf, Redwood_ratecard_Q4_2026.xlsx, SOW_Huntley_Draft.docx.

Quick answers:
- Overage/burst billing: we bill actual consumed tokens above the committed evaluation slab at the burst rate tier. During the eval we can apply a differentiated burst ladder: up to 2x committed throughput billed at 1.25x list rate; 2x-4x billed at 1.75x; >4x billed at 2.5x. Example calc is in the spreadsheet (tab: EvalExample).
- Temporary cap: yes — we can gate billing with a hard cap during the first 30 days. Once you hit the cap, further requests are throttled or routed to a lower-cost compatible model per your preference. We typically suggest a soft alert at 80% and a hard cap you set.
- Invoice example: see Redwood_ratecard_Q4_2026.xlsx; for 2M excess tokens at a 3x spike the sample shows a blended burst multiplier of 1.75 giving X dollars (spreadsheet has line items).

MAP highlights (summary):
- 30-day evaluation period (Dec 1 — Dec 30)
- Success metrics: average p95 latency < 350ms, cost per 1K tokens < target, integration of prefix caching
- Mutual milestones: staging integration (week 1), evaluation load run (week 2), quality review & business sign-off (week 4)
- Billing: evaluation slab (committed tokens), burst ladder as above; 30-day hard cap option available

Next steps: I’ll incorporate a short clause into the SOW to reflect the hard cap and the DocuSign-ready SOW if you confirm the cap value. Would you like procurement’s preferred DocuSign recipient on the SOW now?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415-555-0132
[Attachment: MAP_Huntley_v1.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: Redwood_ratecard_Q4_2026.xlsx (XLSX)]
[Attachment: SOW_Huntley_Draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Eval plan + MAP questions (burst caps / overage rates)

Ben — quick internal note before you finalize:

- I recommend offering a one-time evaluation credit (up to $2k) to cover unexpected burst consumption during onboarding; marketing this as a "first-30-day grace credit" helps reduce friction for procurement.
- Add explicit language to the SOW about the hard cap behavior (throttle vs. fallback to a cheaper model) — procurement will want deterministic behavior.
- Aditya, can you draft a 1-sentence legal-friendly clause for the SOW that preserves our right to suspend excess traffic if the cap is exceeded and defines refund/credit mechanics?

If procurement needs a PO-based billing flow we can accept PO followed by a one-time invoice for the eval slab.

-lb
Lauren Bishop
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
[Internal Note: possible concession approval 2k credit — confirm with sales ops]

From: Olivia Huntley <olivia@huntleyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@huntleyhealth.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Action plan & eval — clarifications on overage policy and burst rate

Ben — thanks for the clear breakdown and attachments. Procurement reviewed the SOW and procurement@huntleyhealth.com asked for two clarifications before we sign: 

1) Hard cap value: we propose a hard cap of $5,000 for the first 30 days. If the cap is reached we prefer requests to be throttled (HTTP 429) rather than fallback to a lower-quality model. Can you confirm Redwood can support that behavior?

2) Burst rate confirmation: procurement asked for a written example with numbers in the SOW itself (they don’t always open spreadsheets). Please include the 3x spike example and the blended multiplier math in the SOW so the PI owner can route.

We are comfortable with the MAP milestones as-is and would accept a one-time eval credit up to $2k to help mitigate risk. Once those two items are reflected we can sign and route the DocuSign back to procurement@huntleyhealth.com.

If you can send the DocuSign-ready SOW with those two edits today, we’ll aim to return it signed by Monday and begin the eval on Dec 8.

Best,
Olivia Huntley
VP Product, Huntley Health
[Attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf (PDF)]
